acceptance_criteria: AC-1 Ordering: newest observation first, then newest entry, then id; independent of read order (rotations and reversal give the same timeline)
AC-2 Correction history: a chain is one entry; the newest version counts; every version stays; a correction to 'not measured' stays missing; a schema 1 supersedes without reason is a correction
AC-3 Entered in error: voids its target; on a correction the previous version counts again; on an original the entry leaves current views and stays in the history view

AC-4 Delete: tombstones the whole fact (all versions) with a deletion time; hidden from current views, shown in the history view; a later correction cannot resurrect it; schema 1 self-deleted records are deleted
AC-5 Conflict: two live corrections of one version are shown as a conflict with both versions; Today shows 'Versions disagree' instead of a number; marking one side entered in error resolves it
AC-6 Record schema 2 rules: amendment needs a target; schema 2 supersedes needs a reason; markers carry no value; only deletions carry deleted_at; schema 1 JSON keeps its exact shape
AC-7 Store integrity: amendments of missing records, markers, or another profile/kind are refused before writing (file unchanged); on replay they are skipped with a warning
AC-8 Use cases: correct / entered in error / delete append exactly one record each (append-only), only on the current version (TARGET_NOT_CURRENT / TARGET_NOT_FOUND), and survive a restart
AC-9 Timeline UI: entries newest first with state and source; correct flow; entered-in-error and delete confirmations explain the difference; history toggle; EN/TR; 320 dp at 2x text without overflow
AC-10 Fixture v1_f003_schema2 (mixed schema 1 and 2) equals the writer's bytes and replays into the expected lineage
